name: php-predictable-random-security-token
attack_scenario: Attacker requests a password reset, observes or predicts the microsecond-seeded uniqid/mt_rand token (or reconstructs the MT state from prior tokens), and forges a valid reset link to hijack any account.
negative_test_hint: request a password reset and submit a token forged from a predicted PRNG value such as "1804289383" and assert it is rejected and that issued tokens are not reproducible from mt_rand or uniqid outputs

exemplar.explanation: uniqid() derives from the microsecond clock and mt_rand()/rand() are non-cryptographic Mersenne Twister PRNGs whose internal state is recoverable from a handful of outputs, so reset or session tokens minted from them can be predicted or brute-forced inside their validity window. random_bytes()/random_int() draw from the operating system CSPRNG, making tokens unguessable.
